content: 编按 人口学上的“下行”在中国已不是预测，而是现实：总人口自2021年见顶后，每年减少三四百万人。美国福特汉姆大学法学院教授明克胜（Carl Minzner）此文的贡献在于，他没有把人口衰退当作单纯的经济问题，而是把它和政治制度的演变放在一起看。他认为，改革时代的中国之所以能把人口红利（劳动年龄人口占比高带来的增长优势）转化为增长，是因为当时高层权力关系与意识形态领域都有一定的开放性，能容纳像农村改革、分税制、国企改制那样代价高昂的政策调整。如今，党的体制回到一人统治，官员习惯于执行中央意志而非解决问题，延迟退休、城乡养老差距等明显的改革议题都被一拖再拖。作者更进一步指出，官方推动的本土主义与传统性别观念，会让婚育和引进外劳都更困难，使人口问题恶化而非缓解；当社会矛盾积累，国家的应对方式是把它“安全化”，也就是把社会问题当作维稳和安全问题处理。他借晚明张居正改革失败、万历怠政、李自成起事作类比，警示中国可能在2030—2040年代面临继承危机与社会断裂叠加的局面。文章最后转向美国，指出生育率下降、反移民和国会僵局同样可能侵蚀一个大国。这一比较的价值在于提醒读者：人口趋势本身不决定命运，决定命运的是制度能否持续地作出纠错和选择。 原文：Carl Minzner, “China’s Long Twilight: Demographic Decline, Political Paralysis, and the Fate of Great Powers,” Foreign Affairs , November/December 2026（网络版发布于2026年10月5日） 链接： https://www.foreignaffairs.com/china/chinas-long-twilight-carl-minzner At the Dongyue Temple in Beijing, February 2026 Maxim Shemetov / Reuters 摘要 1. 人口红利的退潮 改革时代，中国的劳动年龄人口（15—64岁）占比从1978年的57%升至2010年的近75%，支撑了三十年近10%的年增速，经济规模扩大约20倍。 独生子女政策，加上整个东亚共有的社会因素，使中国生育率已连续三十年低于更替水平。更替水平指维持人口规模不变所需的生育率，约为每名妇女生育2.1个孩子。 总人口在2021年以14亿见顶，此后每年减少三四百万，相当于每年少一个洛杉矶。若延续东亚的超低生育率，2040年代每年将减少约1%，即约1000万人。 65岁以上人口占比将从目前的15%翻倍到2040年代的约30%，本世纪后期超过40%。美国同一比例预计从约19%缓升至2060年的略高于23%。 2. 政治倒退：从技术官僚治理到一人统治 作者引用《纽约时报》专栏作者袁莉的说法：美国存在一种“中国羡慕”，即惊叹于中国的AI、电池、光伏和高铁。但他认为表象之下，中国正在经历同样深刻、只是更安静的政治侵蚀。 他列举的个人化统治迹象： 2018年取消国家主席任期限制； 2022年二十大清洗高层并安插亲信； 军队高层反复整肃，2026年连习近平亲自挑选的张又侠也被拿下。 习近平将于2027年开始第四个总书记任期；2032年他将79岁，至今没有接班安排。 作者以农村改革亲历者赵树凯为证：改革时代的突破依赖“高层权力关系和意识形态领域的开放”。 他还对比了两段史实：江泽民授权朱镕基推行1994年分税制；朱镕基不惜数千万人下岗、引发大规模劳工抗议，推动国企改制以加入世贸组织。 今天的情形相反。2022年上海原本尝试精准防疫，但与习近平押上个人威信的“清零”政策冲突，最终演变为两个月封城。时任市委书记李强非但未被问责，反而进入政治局常委会并出任总理。 3. 改革停滞：养老金与城乡鸿沟 中国的退休年龄长期处于世界最低之列：男性60岁，女干部55岁，女工人50岁。中国学者预测，覆盖约5亿人的城镇职工养老金将在2030年代中期耗尽。 2024年才宣布渐进式延迟退休，到2040年完全实施后也只有：男63岁，女干部58岁，女工人55岁。 2022年，约1.38亿城镇退休人员年均养老金6080美元，约为1.75亿农村和流动人口退休者（年均345美元）的18倍。 作者认为，再分配改革迟迟不推，是因为官员更害怕得罪城市既得利益群体（公务员、国企职工、中产），而农村和流动人口缺乏组织动员能力。 4. “明朝重演”：本土主义与性别保守化 作者称，官方警惕“外来文化渗透”，强调“中华优秀传统文化”，推崇女性作为“贤妻良母”的“独特作用”。这些做法在助推一种本土主义（排斥外来人和外来文化）和新传统主义（回到旧家庭和性别规范）的复兴。 他拿明朝作类比。明朝在蒙元统治之后转向内向保守：压制摩尼教等外来信仰，推动少数民族通婚同化，回归理学的女性观。对应的当代现象包括：2010年以来的宗教“中国化”、2026年《民族团结进步促进法》、全国妇联被要求“做好家庭工作”。 2013—2024年，中国新登记结婚数量下降约55%。作者认为，全部由男性组成的政治局只把问题当作激励不足：2021年推出育儿补贴、育儿假，同时限制离婚、堕胎和输精管结扎。这些政策收效甚微，还恶化了性别关系。 5. 移民这条路也被堵上 韩国外籍居民占比已从1990年代初近乎为零升至约5%。中国2010年和2020年两次人口普查中，外籍居民都只占0.1%。 2025年8月，中国推出吸引青年外籍理工人才的新签证（即“K字签证”，这一名称为编者补充）。当月青年失业率为18.9%，网上随即爆发强烈反弹：有人把为政府辩护者骂作“汉奸”，有人担心印度工程师抢工作、抢婚恋对象。一年多后，仍无该签证实际签发的报道。 作者认为，男女之间、中外之间、城乡之间的社会裂痕，将在2049年建政百年前进一步加深。 6. “定时炸弹”：社会问题的安全化 作者不完全认同“中国会在下行前冒险攻台”的“理性赌博论”，即 Brands 与 Beckley 在《危险地带》（ Danger Zone ）中的观点。他认为，更大的风险是孤立的年迈领导人严重误判，类比普京2022年入侵乌克兰、特朗普2026年对伊朗开战。 但他认为更深的风险在内部。2023年成立的中央社会工作部负责关注“四缺”人员（无配偶子女、无工作或稳定收入、无正常社交、无房车等资产）和“五失”人员（投资失败、事业或人生受挫、情绪失衡、精神疾病、人际关系失败），将其视为可能制造恶性事件的安全隐患。作者举的例子是2024年11月一名62岁男子因离婚财产分割不满驾车冲撞人群、致数十人死亡。 作者预计，未来人口变化带来的社会问题都会被“安全化”，即当作安全和维稳问题处理，依靠监控和网格化管理（把城乡划成小格、由专人包干监控的基层治理方式）来压住。 晚明的类比： 张居正试图让士绅承担更多税负，1582年死后改革被推翻 万历皇帝与官僚长期对峙，导致朝政瘫痪； 1620年代裁撤驿站，使驿卒李自成失业，后来他率领饥民起事，1644年推翻明朝。 当代的对应迹象： 地方财政吃紧，拖欠教师和公务员工资； 城乡居民医保保费二十年来年均上涨20%，约8300万人近年退保。 7. 对美国的警示 作者主张，美国应回应中国的具体威胁，但不应把对华竞争渲染成“文明生存之战”，否则正好替北京转嫁内部不满。 他指出，过度的对华猜疑已伤害美国自身：麦卡锡时代逼走了钱学森；今天收紧签证、多州立法禁止中国公民购地，2025年国际学生入学人数下降17%。 美国生育率自2008年起低于更替水平，又在收紧移民，2027年公布的数据可能显示美国人口史上首次下降。国会平均年龄是有记录以来第三高，政府停摆已成常态，贫富差距也与中国相当。 作者的结论：人口危机不是宿命，而是一连串选择的累积。习近平治下的中国已失去选择的余地，美国仍然可以作出不同选择。

title: Expanding Taiwan’s Resistance Area Complex by way of Japan and the Philippines

content:
简介 台湾存在战略纵深问题。如果遭到入侵，它没有陆地边界，没有邻国可以撤退，也没有腹地可以争取时间。就台湾而言，在中国登陆后幸存下来的军队和抵抗力量将在地理上受到压缩，并在靠近占领军的地方作战，无处可退。在台湾的情况下，“留守部队”的想法，即那些旨在隐藏、生存并最终在前进的敌人的后方地区行动的部队，即使不是不可能，也是极具挑战性的。该岛的孤立将使得进口武器、医疗用品、外国战士和通讯设备变得困难，即使存在运送这些物品的政治意愿。台湾的地理位置既是抵御入侵的防御资产，也是抵御占领的不利条件。 Background Information Planning Taiwan’s physical resistance architecture across time and space, prior to invasion, demands creativity. American doctrine is informative in this case but not particularly well-suited to the island’s one-of-a-kind situation.美国陆军特种部队非常规战争条令，包括野战手册 3-05.201，将“区域综合体”定义为秘密的、分散的设施网络，为抵抗运动提供安全、控制、分散和灵活性，实际上是由抵抗运动本身建立和控制的解放区。
手册建议，该地区综合体应包括安全系统、大本营（这在台湾不太可能，但安全屋是可能且需要的）、通信、后勤、医疗设施、补给库、训练区以及逃生和恢复机制。它将综合体细分为外部和内部安全区，围绕抵抗区指挥部建立，在台湾可能会分散而不是合并。该理论模型假设了连续的、可扩展的地面：抵抗力量可以进入的区域，用于将其外部区域与其内部区域分开，并在到达指挥单元之前吸收压力。台湾可以规划和组织一个内部地带。实际上，它无法建造学说所假设的与它并肩而立的外部世界，因为没有毗邻的领土可以放置它。不幸的是，对于台湾来说，人民是“地理的囚徒”，正如蒂姆·马歇尔的同名著作所暗示的那样。外部安全区有几项工作通常与抵抗组织在同一块土地上进行：组织和发展战士和民事支持基础设施，作为新兵来源，提供第一线的深入安全和警报，并向抵抗组织指挥部提供有关区域内敌方活动的及时、准确的情报。
该区域的成员筛选、选择和训练新的抵抗组织成员，其中最有能力的进入正规武装部队，而与他们并肩建立的文职支援部队则收集情报并向抵抗区域指挥单元提供后勤和心理行动支持。该条令中没有一个假设假设外部区域与其支持的部队隔着开阔的水域。台湾的地理位置迫使我们适应而不是放弃这一概念：志愿者的招募和审查、中国海军通过海峡行动的情报收集，以及对地区指挥单位的后勤和通信支持都发生了变化。这些功能必须在医生允许的距离内执行

Introduction Taiwan has a strategic depth problem. If invaded, it has no land border, no neighboring state to retreat into, and no hinterland to buy time. In the case of Taiwan, military and resistance forces that survive a Chinese landing would be geographically compressed and operating in close proximity to the occupying forces, with nowhere to fall back. The idea of “ stay-behind forces ,” those intended to hide, survive, and eventually operate in the rear area of an advancing enemy, is extremely challenging – if not impossible – in the Taiwan scenario. The island’s isolation would make it difficult to import weapons, medical supplies, foreign fighters, and communications equipment, even where the political will to send them existed. Taiwan’s geography is both a defensive asset against invasion and a liability against occupation. Background Information Planning Taiwan’s physical resistance architecture across time and space, prior to invasion, demands creativity. American doctrine is informative in this case but not particularly well-suited to the island’s one-of-a-kind situation. US Army Special Forces Unconventional Warfare doctrine, including Field Manual 3-05.201 , defines an “area complex” as a clandestine, dispersed network of facilities that gives a resistance movement security, control, dispersion, and flexibility, in effect, a liberated zone built and held by the resistance itself. The manuals recommend that the area complex include a security system, base camps (which will be unlikely in Taiwan, but safehouses will be possible and needed), communications, logistics, medical facilities, supply caches, training areas, and escape and recovery mechanisms. It subdivides the complex into an outer and an inner security zone, built around the resistance area command, which would likely be distributed rather than consolidated in Taiwan. The doctrinal model assumes contiguous, expandable ground: territory a resistance force can grow into, use to separate its outer zone from its inner one, and absorb pressure before it reaches command cells. Taiwan can plan and organize an inner zone. Practically, it cannot build the outer one that doctrine assumes sits alongside it, because there is no adjoining territory to put it in. Unfortunately for Taiwan, the people are “prisoners of geography,” as Tim Marshall’s book of the same name suggests. The outer security zone has several jobs that normally happen on the same landmass as the resistance itself: organizing and developing fighters and civilian support infrastructure, serving as a source of recruits, providing the first line of in-depth security and warning, and feeding the resistance area command cells with timely, accurate intelligence on enemy activity within the zone. Members in that zone screen, select, and train new resistance members, with the most capable moving into the regular armed element, while the civilian support element, built alongside them, gathers intelligence and delivers logistical and psychological operations support to resistance area command cells. None of that doctrine assumes the outer zone sits across open water from the force it supports. Taiwan’s geography forces an adaptation rather than an abandonment of the concept: recruitment and vetting of volunteers, intelligence collection on Chinese naval movements through the straits, and logistics and communications support to area command cells all shift. These functions must be performed at a distance that the doctrine never anticipated. Miyako Strait (Image Credit: The Straits Times) Japan and the Philippines Japan and the Philippines are where the missing outer zone of the area complex can go. In fact, they may be the only realistic locations immediately adjacent to Taiwan that can perform that function. While Guam, Palau, Okinawa, and other places may play a role, the requirement here is to develop locations that can serve as immediate, geographically close extensions of the resistance area complex. Yonaguni Island (Image Credit: South China Morning Post) Both countries are already part of the conversation about a Taiwan contingency, and both have said so in their own words rather than having the role assigned to them by outsiders. Sanae Takaichi, Japan’s Prime Minister, told Japan’s parliament on November 7, 2025, that China’s use of armed force against Taiwan could constitute what Japanese law calls a “survival-threatening situation,” the threshold that permits Japan to exercise collective self-defense. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said in August 2025 that a war over Taiwan would draw the Philippines into the conflict regardless of its own preferences, citing proximity and the roughly 180,000 Filipinos residing on the island, and that hope is not a plan. To be clear, neither statement commits either government to a specific military role. The Bashi Channel and Batanes Islands (Image Credit: Robert Luster, StongerNavy.org) Just as geography limits maneuver depth on the island itself, it also narrows where the expanded area complex, depth-by-proxy, could realistically land. Japan’s southwestern Sakishima Islands, particularly Yonaguni, sit 110 kilometers from Taiwan and overlook the Miyako Strait, one of the two principal maritime corridors through which the PLA Navy would seek access to the Western Pacific during a Taiwan conflict. The Philippines’ Batanes Islands sit across the Bashi Channel from Taiwan’s Orchid Island, the second passage , which is 80 kilometers wide . Note that Osumi Strait and Tokara Gap are also available for limited traffic, but for Taiwan operations, the Miyako Strait and Bashi Channel are by far the two principal deep-water exits. Japan is already fortifying Yonaguni with missiles and sensors, while the Philippines has rehearsed rapid anti-ship missile deployments to Batanes during joint exercises with the United States. In addition to the geography requirements of the area complex equation, what is also missing is a special operations mission that’s built to move people, equipment, and information through those same two islands into an occupied Taiwan, and to keep moving them for the resistance once a blockade is in place. Such a mission could include at least four functions. The Resistance Mission The first is communications relay. China has already shown a willingness to sever Taiwan’s connectivity through means short of war: a Chinese-owned vessel was accused of cutting a fiber-optic cable near Keelung Harbor in January 2025, following earlier damage to cables serving Taiwan’s Matsu Islands in 2023. In an actual invasion, isolating Taiwan from the outside world would be an early objective. Relay infrastructure staged on Yonaguni and Batanes, built and rehearsed in peacetime, could keep resistance networks and civilian authorities in contact with the outside world after primary infrastructure fails. The second is unmanned insertion, extraction, and resupply, which helps address the logistics and supply caches that doctrine expects an area complex to maintain internally. Small unmanned surface vessels and unmanned aerial systems, launched at night from Batanes or the Sakishima Islands and running beneath a blockade line, are within current technical reach. This is a mission-planning, basing, and personnel management problem more than a technology problem. Building local relationships, expertise, and staging sites is a peacetime preparation task that retired Special Forces Colonel Brian Petit argued requires a long-dwell, host-embedded advisory presence. Applied to the area-complex concept proposed in this paper, Petit’s idea of a persistent advisory mission adapted to this paper would include US Special Forces not only in Taiwan, but also on the two islands and other locations that would run the resistance pipeline once Taiwan is cut off. An Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) Penetrates A Chinese Blockade with Ammunition, Medical, and Communication Supplies for The Resistance (Fictional Image. Image Credit: Grok AI) The third is facilitating the introduction of foreign volunteers who want to fight for Taiwan, which supports the doctrinal escape-and-recovery mechanism in reverse: instead of moving evaders out of denied territory, the same tradecraft moves vetted personnel in. Ukraine’s International Legion drew thousands of foreign fighters within weeks of the 2022 Russian invasion, staging through Poland and other neighboring states that were not themselves combatants. Taiwan has no land border and no neighbor that could serve that role by geographic accident. Japan and the Philippines are plausible staging grounds for screening, inserting, and, if necessary, extracting foreign volunteers. A fourth function is kinetic interdiction of Chinese naval forces from Japanese or Philippine soil. This function is more challenging to plan, organize, and train during peacetime because of the obvious political sensitivity. Japan’s “survival-threatening situation” authority and the Philippines’ Mutual Defense Treaty with the United States both provide a legal path to this kind of involvement. But activation would likely occur only once Tokyo or Manila has determined that it is already a party to the conflict and pre-determined thresholds have been crossed. Treating Japan and the Philippines as two more US Special Forces advisory locations alongside Taiwan introduces a harder problem: what sustains a pipeline like this over the years is whether the people running it understand how all three nodes connect, rather than knowing only their own. Not unlike Petit’s concept for Green Berets on long-term Taiwan rotations, a dedicated cadre in this model would instead rotate its personnel sequentially through all three countries, on tours lasting several years each rather than a series of unrelated deployments in which entire teams move in and out at the same time. Optimally, this would include the rotation of not just American advisors but also Japanese, Philippine, and Taiwanese operators. An operator serves a tour in the Philippines, then Japan, then Taiwan, for example, or some ordering suited to the mission, carrying forward what worked in one place and testing it against the next. The result is a body of institutional knowledge about running the resistance pipeline that travels with the people who built it, rather than resetting with every new team that arrives. Foreign Fighters Infiltrate Taiwan to Assist the Resistance (Fictional Image. Image Credit: Google Gemini) Objections Three potential objections to this proposal deserve acknowledgment. The first is consent. Takaichi’s and Marcos’s statements support self-defense and the evacuation of their own nationals. In January 2026, Japan and the Philippines signed a new defense pact amid growing Chinese aggression. Despite this, these actions cannot be interpreted as consent to host an active pipeline built to resupply and reinforce a resistance movement within a state whose government does not formally recognize it. No one should treat public statements from these leaders as a blank check, but the positions from both may serve as a starting point for an expansion of activity. The second is provocation. Beijing’s response to one sentence from Takaichi in the Diet, a halt on Japanese seafood imports , travel advisories, and roughly 500,000 canceled airline tickets , shows how little China needs before retaliating economically. A standing cadre and physical infrastructure on Yonaguni and Batanes will draw an exponentially sharper reaction. The third objection is effectiveness. The Bashi Channel and Miyako Strait are dense, monitored waterways, and unmanned traffic crossing them in wartime will likely be detected and attributed, no matter how careful the tradecraft is, which raises a fair question about whether the pipeline can move enough volume to matter, or perhaps what other functions it may accomplish. Addressing issues related to consent and provocation will be consequential to the success or failure of this proposal. Whether this happens before or after the invasion is also significant. If the Philippines and Japan, or perhaps only one, consider the costs of escalation with China to be borne as a result of embracing this area-complex construct in peacetime, and weigh them against the benefits to be gained for their country in war, they may conclude that the return on investment is worth it. As mentioned earlier, leaders of both countries have articulated that a fight for Taiwan will not be just about Taiwan but will have regional implications, including for their countries. Admittedly, this is not a mitigation of negative costs so much as an acceptance of them. As for the risks associated with establishing communications relay functions and the resistance cadre developing personal relationships on the ground on these adjacent islands, these activities also create similar political and diplomatic costs to those mentioned above. There are genuine, dual-use benefits to establishing communication mechanisms and human-to-human trust networks that come with persistent engagement on these islands, extending beyond conflict or preparation for conflict. Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief preparation, for example, is the most honest example of a capability that would benefit from establishing these systems now. The reality is, however, that building these capabilities prior to invasion may invite retaliation from China. Strategic ambiguity, a constant theme for nearly every country in the world regarding Taiwan, is the first option for the Philippines and Japan as it pursues dual-use preparations discussed here. Or, secondly, both countries may decide to clearly declare their willingness to begin preparing for conflict out of genuine concern for their national security. Or, a third option is that establishing such resistance-support mechanisms may not occur until after hostilities have broken out, and leaders are forced to make hard decisions. The latter outcome doesn’t mean the expanded area complex doesn’t become an operational reality, but it may mean it isn’t optimally planned and exercised. The higher-risk, higher-signature functions involved with the expanded area complex, unmanned insertion runs, and foreign fighter staging become branch plans that would almost certainly not activate until Tokyo or Manila has crossed its own legal thresholds, the same gating already applied to kinetic interdiction. The intent of this paper is not to presuppose what Tokyo or Manila will do or to assume the level of risk these countries are willing to take, but rather to put forth a resistance-support concept and acknowledge the costs associated with it. How these two countries proceed will ultimately be based on what they perceive best for their own survival, not anyone else’s. Effectiveness is a different kind of problem, since it isn’t a matter of managing political risk but of surviving physical detection. There are at least three approaches as to what “success” actually means for this expanded area complex. There is the ambitious one in which the pipeline sustains the resistance movement; the modest one in which the network survives and complicates the enemy’s occupation; and the third, a combination of the two. As for sustaining the resistance itself, it is important to remember that this expanded area complex is the terrestrial-based manifestation of the complex. While the inner and outer zones are where a considerable amount of physical support originates, there will also be maritime (surface and sub-surface), air, space-based, and virtual support to the resistance. Ideally, all of these lines of effort will be well orchestrated. The point here is that it is not only the land-based resistance area complex on Japanese and Philippine islands that will be tasked with supporting the resistance. As for disruption, history provides a useful example. Detachment A, the Cold War Special Forces unit that ran stay-behind operations in West Berlin, never had full deniability, surrounded as it was by Soviet and East German intelligence services, and its value lay in persistence and complication rather than invisibility. This pipeline’s job will include a similar mission: survive attrition and impose cost. In reality, the expanded resistance area complex, together with the other support efforts mentioned, will serve several functions simultaneously. Furthermore, depending on the reality on the ground, one part of the network may serve one function while another serves a different purpose. Summary This paper provides a modern adaptation of the doctrinal “area complex” needed to support resistance on an island facing a realistic threat of invasion and occupation. The overarching strategic concept is outlined here, but the operational and tactical realities of the architecture require additional scrutiny. The idea of a Chinese invasion is often discussed among the US, Taiwan, Japan, the Philippines, and other like-minded partners. The integration of mechanisms across international borders to build depth of resistance to compensate for geographic shortfalls, however, is not explored in practical terms, as it is here. Expanding the area complex’s footprint on the ground is possible if the aperture is spread onto two pieces of partner territory that are not Taiwan’s own. Disclaimer: The views expressed here are the author’s alone and do not reflect the official policy or position of the US Government or the Department of War. The post Expanding Taiwan’s Resistance Area Complex by way of Japan and the Philippines appeared first on Small Wars Journal by Arizona State University .

title: 台湾：支持美光工人罢工
source: 中国劳工论坛 China Worker
summary: 这场斗争也是全体工人的斗争 陈延年 国际社会主义道路（ISA）台湾 10月7日，台湾美光晶圆科技企业工会（桃园工会）正式发布罢工投票结果。在全体会员高达89.1%的高参与率下，工会以高达99.1%的压倒性同意率正式取得合法罢工权。这不仅是美光建厂以来的首次，更是台湾半导体与高科技产业史上的首例合法罢工授权事件，并已正式宣布于10月22日（周四）发动为期一天的首波实际罢工行动，以声援会员人数已增至11,000人（覆蓋率近90%）的台中工会。 美光正如许多跨国资本，只是与其他科技
content: 这场斗争也是全体工人的斗争 陈延年 国际社会主义道路（ISA）台湾 10月7日，台湾美光晶圆科技企业工会（桃园工会）正式发布罢工投票结果。在全体会员高达89.1%的高参与率下，工会以高达99.1%的压倒性同意率正式取得合法罢工权。这不仅是美光建厂以来的首次，更是台湾半导体与高科技产业史上的首例合法罢工授权事件，并已正式宣布于10月22日（周四）发动为期一天的首波实际罢工行动，以声援会员人数已增至11,000人（覆蓋率近90%）的台中工会。 美光正如许多跨国资本，只是与其他科技巨头比赛谁能从劳工身上榨取最多血汗。当前会发起罢工不是没有原因的。随着生成式AI爆发，美光在高频宽记忆体（HBM）与高阶DRAM等领域赚取了暴利，最新2026会计年度（FY2026）财报显示全年营收冲上1,332亿美元历史纪录，且2027年全年HBM高阶产能早已被客户预订一空。 基层劳工被压榨 然而，2023年记忆体寒冬期间，台湾厂区即便仍有获利，基层劳工却依然遭到美光总公司要求齐头式裁员10%并全面冻结奖金。如今面对公司的空前荣景，底薪与分红却被刻意压制。资方将高阶主管与基层员工的薪酬差距拉大到令人发指的地步：2025年美光全年净利暴增逾10倍达85亿美元，但黑箱的IPP绩效奖金制度却仅给出93.9%的达成率系数（「勿忘93.9」），台湾员工实际领取的绩效奖金仅约2.6个月薪资，而执行长的年度现金绩效奖励却高达32.4个月！ 在2025年限制型股票奖励（RSA）分配上，全球员工平均仅获约207股，执行长却得83,015股，差距高达400倍（2023年亏损裁员期间差距更达570倍）！而台湾员工在限制型股票单位（RSU）的覆蓋率过往更仅有约40%，远低于美国厂区的近100%。劳工多年付出的心血遭到资方高层无情地窃取。 美光的南韩竞争对手如三星电子与SK海力士，在面临强大工会罢工威胁后，皆已将年度营业利益的10.5%至12%（三星）与10%（SK海力士）明确化作为分润基础。反观台湾美光，资方却拒绝建立透明的「营业利益15%常态化按季分润制」，反而在9月11日未经协商片面宣布每人100万新台币的「一次性感谢金」，并以基层作业员约3万元的极低底薪为分母，包装出「整体薪酬最高68个月」的公关话术（月薪6万元者实领折算仅约25.45个月），实质新增奖酬仅占公司营业利益约4.4%，企图以此收买基层、瓦解罢工动能。 资方之所以敢如此傲慢，实际上是因为台湾长期缺乏足以迫使科技资本家低头的强大工会运动。台湾美光约15,000名员工仅占全球逾6万名人力约四分之一，却贡献了全球高达50%～60%以上的DRAM与先进记忆体产能。这一切丰厚利润与晶圆产出，明明都是工人血汗劳动与日夜轮班的结晶，如今管理层却向华尔街承诺在扣除资本支出后，将100%超额自由现金流全数用于扩大库藏股回购以回馈股东与推升股价，沦为华尔街与高层予取予求的禁脔。 「摸头妥协」 资方在先前的劳资协商中毫无诚意，多次将决策推托给10月8日至9日召开的美国总公司董事会；然而董事会结束已超过10天，资方仍未针对分润金额与制度提出任何具体对案，仅以「48周年餐食补助」与缺货的「PayEasy礼品」敷衍塞责。10月15日美光台中先进封装测试二厂（AATT2）启用时，美光全球营运长甚至完全避谈罢工争议。 然而，10月21日台湾美光与台中工会突袭发布联合声明，宣布双方已正式签署劳资协议，并撤回原订22日的调解程序。美光所谓的2027会计年度新薪酬制度，不仅将季度利润奖金强制拆分为「50%现金、50%须锁闭一年归属的股票」，更在奖金池计算中埋下陷阱：规定每季必须「先扣除／预留下一季资本支出所需资金」后，才计算员工利润奖金，且未透明公开获利提拨比例公式。这根本是把公司疯狂扩厂的财务压力，直接转嫁到员工的奖金池。当基层奖金被压缩的同时，美国高层和华尔街股东却靠着公司买回库藏股、拉抬股价，继续爽领巨额利润！而原先工会要求的今年度一次性大额现金补偿与四大诉求则全数落空。 这起未经民主程序、未公开协议文本、更未经会员大会投票表决的「摸头妥协」，引爆台中工会内部1.1万名基层会员的愤慨。基层劳工痛批：「四大诉求一个都没有达到怎么会妥协？成员对内容完全不知情，也没有带回来民主投票！」面对干部以「明天开奖就知道为什么够了」敷衍，会员已发起线上紧急连署，要求撤销原签约授权、完整公开最终文本，并依《工会法》门槛要求召开临时会员大会重新审议。 绝不接受背叛 更有甚者，台中工会干部在21日单独与资方签约撤回调解，不仅背弃了此前与桃园工会「双厂同进退、共同列席谈判」的盟约，更让已握有罢工权、准备在22日发动一日警告性罢工以声援台中的桃园工会陷入孤立。而美光台湾将桃园与台中登记为两家独立公司法人的壁垒，让资方有空间分流谈判，又遭到少数干部在保密条款下「先斩后奏」地代表签约，这些都暴露出资方借由分化个别厂场工会、以不透明协议试图瓦解劳动阶级团结的惯用伎俩。这场突如其来的妥协风波，再次血淋淋地证明资本家绝不会自动施舍，而官僚化的密室协商更只会出卖工人的血汗成果。■ 国际社会主义道路主张： 支持台中美光基层会员行使民主权利，坚决拒绝保密黑箱！声援台中厂会员发起的连署行动，要求立即公开劳资协议最终文本，并召开临时会员大会进行实质审议与民主投票；反对少数干部在密室中代表超过一万名成员签署协议。 支持桃园工会的罢工抗争，两厂工人应拒绝被各个击破！针对资方刻意利用法人壁垒与各厂协商时间差进行的分化，我们呼吁桃园工会继续捍卫基层权益，同时支援台中工会会员打破黑箱；工人的权利必须靠集体动员与公开透明的争取，拒绝打了折扣的摸头方案。 建设民主决策、积极斗争的工会组织！各厂工会干部必须受到全体会员民主授权与罢免权的严格监督。同时保护罢工工人与工会干部不被资方秋后算帐，阻止资方在AI泡沫破裂时要工人承担苦果。 动员群众集会，桃园与台中两厂工人应共同讨论并投票制定运动的下一步。并协调跨企业的工人共同行动，串联台积电等半导体产业劳工，打破资方的工会禁令组织团结斗争，不被老板们各个击破，共同对抗台湾高科技业普遍长工时与分红不透明的剥削。 建设群众斗争，打破台湾现有反民主亲资方的工会组织门槛、政治罢工禁令与跨企业联合罢工限制。支持国际工人发起协调斗争，连结美光全球各厂区以及南韩三星、SK海力士等的跨国科技工人，反对资方任何企图分化、差别对待不同国籍劳工的手段。 這篇文章 台湾：支持美光工人罢工 最早出現於 中国劳工论坛 China Worker 。

title: Lawmakers press Air Force on civilian cuts at China aerospace institute
zh_title: 立法者向空军施压，要求削减中国航天研究院的文职人员
summary: 众议院中国共产党特别委员会的议员们正在敦促空军就其削减中国航天研究院所有文职职位的决定做出答复。在 11 月 4 日致空军部长特洛伊·梅克 (Troy Meink) 的信中，密歇根州共和党主席约翰·穆勒纳尔 (John Moolenaar) 和加利福尼亚州民主党高级成员罗·卡纳 (Ro Khanna) 要求在 11 月 20 日之前向空军部长特洛伊·梅克 (Troy Meink) 通报该机构（CASI）的资源配置和人事决策。 CASI 隶属于空军大学，负责管理空军军官学校和士兵学校。 “资源不足的 CASI 使命可能会削弱
content:
众议院中国共产党特别委员会的议员们正在敦促空军就其削减中国航天研究院所有文职职位的决定做出答复。在 11 月 4 日致空军部长特洛伊·梅克 (Troy Meink) 的信中，密歇根州共和党主席约翰·穆勒纳尔 (John Moolenaar) 和加利福尼亚州民主党高级成员罗·卡纳 (Ro Khanna) 要求在 11 月 20 日之前向空军部长特洛伊·梅克 (Troy Meink) 通报该机构（CASI）的资源配置和人事决策。 CASI 隶属于空军大学，负责管理空军军官学校和士兵学校。议员们写道：“CASI 的任务资源不足可能会削弱军事领导人和文职决策者了解中国航空航天战略和能力的能力，进而阻止北京在军事冲突中使用它们。” “鉴于中国不断努力迅速实现其航空航天部队现代化，同时扩大其在印度-太平洋地区的侵略活动，任何此类专业知识的潜在损失都特别令人担忧。”该特别委员会发布的这封信称，如果没有 CASI 的内部专家，空军和其他机构可能不得不求助于成本高昂的外部承包商。
报告还表示，了解中国人民解放军（PLA）的能力对于遏制冲突至关重要，并且援引 CASI 的章程，对于“提高（美国）在战略竞争中取得成功的能力”至关重要。 CASI主任布伦丹·马尔瓦尼周五告诉《防务新闻》，对该研究所的官方评论现在必须通过管理空军大学的航空教育和训练司令部的公共事务，或来自空军大学本身。 作为一名普通公民，马尔瓦尼表示，他不了解该委员会的计划，但“非常高兴看到国会领导层以完全两党合作的方式行事，表现出强有力的支持”，即使在中期选举季节也是如此。他说：“我很高兴 CASI 的成就和贡献得到了整个党派和政府的高度重视。”马尔瓦尼说，两名 CASI 文职人员已经离开，他们的职位现已取消，无法再填补。空军发言人告诉《防务新闻》，该部门“将直接向委员会做出回应”。该发言人没有回答有关空军 CASI 计划或是否会重新填补空缺职位的问题。目前尚不清楚自 10 月 1 日以来是否有额外的军事人员被分配到该研究所。
议员们在写给梅克的信之前，空军于 9 月份做出了决定，即作为航空教育和训练司令部正在进行的文职重组的一部分，将不再向 CASI 分配文职职位。空军发言人当时告诉《防务新闻》，“CASI 的任务仍在继续，该组织利用指定的军人来实现其目标。”  马尔瓦尼在 9 月份对这一举措进行了不同的描述，称取消该研究所的所有文职职位“实际上是结束了 CASI”。他说，没有任何军事职位受到影响，并指出该研究所有两个军士长职位和一个副职位一年多来一直空缺。当被问及文职人员的削减将如何影响 CASI 的研究时，马尔瓦尼说，“所有研究一直都是由文职人员完成的。”马尔瓦尼在 9 月份表示，此次削减“与 CASI 的使命无关”，但源于以下事实

【原文 English Original】
Lawmakers on the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party are pressing the Air Force for answers on its decision to cut all civilian positions at the service’s China Aerospace Studies Institute. In a Nov. 4 letter to Air Force Secretary Troy Meink, Chairman John Moolenaar, R-Mich., and Ranking Member Ro Khanna, D-Calif., requested a briefing by Nov. 20 on the service’s resourcing and personnel decisions for the institute, known as CASI. CASI falls under Air University, which oversees the Air Force’s officer and enlisted schools. “Under-resourcing CASI’s mission could risk undermining the ability of military leaders and civilian policymakers to understand the PRC’s aerospace strategy and capabilities and, by extension, deter Beijing from using them in a military conflict,” the lawmakers wrote. “Any potential loss of such expertise is particularly worrisome given the PRC’s continued efforts to rapidly modernize its aerospace forces while expanding its aggressive activities in the Indo-Pacific region.” The letter, posted by the select committee , said that without CASI’s in-house experts, the Air Force and other agencies would presumably have to turn to costly outside contractors. It also said understanding the capabilities of China’s People’s Liberation Army, or PLA, is critical for deterring conflict and, citing CASI’s charter , for “improving [the U.S.] ability to be successful in strategic competition.” CASI Director Brendan Mulvaney told Defense News Friday that official comment on the institute now must come through public affairs at Air Education and Training Command, which runs Air University, or from Air University itself.  Speaking as a private citizen, Mulvaney said he did not know about the committee’s plans but was “extremely pleased to see that Congressional Leadership acted in a fully bipartisan manner, showing strong support,” even during the midterm election season. “I am gratified that the accomplishments and contributions made by CASI are highly valued across the aisle and across the government,” he said. Two CASI civilians have already left, Mulvaney said, and their now-defunded positions cannot be refilled. An Air Force spokesperson told Defense News that the service “will respond directly to the committee.” The spokesperson did not answer questions about the Air Force’s plans for CASI or whether vacated positions would be refilled. It is unclear whether any additional military personnel have been assigned to the institute since Oct. 1. The lawmakers’ letter to Meink follows the Air Force’s decision, confirmed in September, that civilian positions would no longer be assigned to CASI as part of an ongoing civilian restructure within Air Education and Training Command.  An Air Force spokesperson told Defense News at the time that “the CASI mission continues, with the organization leveraging assigned military service members to accomplish its objectives.”  Mulvaney described the move differently in September, saying that eliminating all of the institute’s civilian positions was “effectively ending CASI.” No military positions are affected, he said, noting the institute has two master sergeant positions and a deputy position that has remained unfilled for over a year. Asked how the civilian cuts would affect CASI’s research, Mulvaney said, “All of the research has always been done by the civilian personnel.” The cut “had nothing to do with CASI’s mission,” Mulvaney said in September, but stemmed from the fact that the institute does not produce professional military education graduates, Air University’s primary mission. Asked whether another organization would take on CASI’s China aerospace research, Mulvaney said, “Nothing has been identified.” In a Sept. 22 statement , later removed from Air University’s website, Mulvaney said Air University had “decided to close” CASI and that all of its civilian positions would go into unfunded status Oct. 1. Employees would keep working and getting paid in “surplus” status while they looked for new jobs, he said, adding, “I will do my best to make sure they all land someplace that will truly appreciate their talents.” Mulvaney said, “CASI has commitments that it has made and will honor, to the best of our ability, through at least March of 2027.” Once the civilians leave, he said, “CASI will close.” CASI was established in 2017, formally chartered June 15, 2021, and tasked with studying “everything that flies” in China. CASI’s research is unclassified by design, drawing on publicly available Chinese-language sources. It also runs a free three-day PLA Fundamentals course, most recently in August, according to the lawmakers’ letter. The biennial CASI Conference, held in May at National Defense University, drew more than 250 attendees and featured the release of the fifth edition of CASI’s “PLA Aerospace Power” primer. In 2025, nearly 80,000 people visited CASI’s website and downloaded more than 50,000 reports, according to the institute. Mulvaney has said the CASI cuts do not affect the Navy’s China Maritime Studies Institute, the Army War College’s China Landpower Studies Center or the Marine Corps War College’s China Warfighting Initiative.

Skip to news navigation, settings and search
Posted Fri 6 Nov 2026 at 1:50pmFri 6 Nov 2026 at 1:50pmFri 6 Nov 2026 at 1:50pm
去年中国灵活就业人员数量已超过2亿人。 (AP:Andy Wong)
与许多中国零工经济从业者一样，自由摄影师阿梅（Ah May）未来退休可能无法依靠养老金。
她经常四处跑，收入并不稳定，负担不起全部费用每月千元人民币（约213澳元）的中国“社会保险”。
“对我来说有一点贵了。我目前收入不高，没有办法交上，”阿梅说。出于隐私考虑，她要求媒体仅使用她的英文名字。
中国面向城镇劳动者的社会保障网络采用保险制模式，要求参保人或其雇主持续缴费。
该体系包括医疗、养老、失业、工伤和生育保险等组成部分。
雇主为员工缴纳社保是法定义务，而个体经营者则可自愿选择是否参保。
今年10月，时任人力资源和社会保障部副部长李忠表示，政府将利用大数据识别未参保人员。
他说，目标是建立一个“更加优化更可持续”的社会保障网，并使其“更密、更牢靠”。
自11月1日起，对于未依法缴纳社保的雇主，处罚标准也已统一，最高可处以应缴保险费用三倍的罚款。
经济学家认为，将社会保障网络覆盖至更多人群，可以使民众减少应急储蓄，从而提振家庭消费支出。
阿梅目前只缴纳医保部分，每月需支付数百元，这已经占了她月收入中的很大一部分。她认为，如果完全自费承担医疗开支，成本会更高。
她表示，自己也希望拥有养老保险保障，但看不到能够负担得起的办法。
“除非有一些福利补贴的政策[缴纳完整保险费用]。”她说。
不少人表示，自己承担不起全部社保费用。 (AP: Mark Schiefelbein)
根据全国人大2025年12月发布的一份报告，中国有超过2亿人从事灵活就业。
这一群体包括自由职业者，以及通过各类应用程序和网站提供劳务、服务或商品的个体平台劳动者。
官方媒体《中国青年报》今年早些时候发布的一项针对1400名平台劳动者的调查显示，在35岁以下受访者中，77%表示愿意自行缴费参加社会保险。
一些年轻人表示，退休年龄提高，使他们对缴纳养老保险是否划算产生了疑虑。 (Reuters: Tingshu Wang)
然而，该调查还发现，真正足额缴纳社保的年轻平台劳动者仅约占17%。
一些灵活就业人员和个体经营者由于无法确定30年后的情况，在20多岁或30多岁时选择不缴纳养老保险。
独立从事金融产品交易的李先生（Lucian Li）便是其中之一。
“自己做交易这么多年，我觉得这个收益率远远超社保。”
悉尼新南威尔士大学（UNSW Sydney）社会政策教授李秉勤表示，政府这些年来一直在逐步加强对未依法缴纳社保费企业的执法力度。
2025年，中国最高法院裁定，企业与员工之间为了节约成本而放弃缴纳社保的私下协议无效。
然而，李教授指出，对企业处以罚款以及让更多人加入社保体系，并不能解决中国社会保障制度面临的根本挑战。
中国人口老龄化意味着缴纳养老金的劳动年龄人口不断减少，而领取养老金的老年人口持续增加。
根据中国国家统计局数据，中国60岁及以上人口已达3.23亿，占总人口约23%。
预计到2030年，这一数字将增至约3.9亿，而劳动年龄人口则将进一步缩减。
李教授表示，中国学者早在2019年就曾提出，对企业职工养老基金而言，到2028年前后可能开始出现收不抵支，并在2035年前后耗尽结余。
“后续更新研究认为，延迟退休政策可能将这一时间点推迟8至9年，”她说。
自2025年起，中国政府开始在15年期限内逐步提高法定退休年龄：蓝领女性由50岁提高至55岁，白领女性由55岁提高至58岁，男性则由60岁提高至63岁。
“[中国社保体系]短期内不存在支付危机，但确实面临现实的结构性[人口]压力。”她说。

title: ‘Truly reflective of his offence’: Police welcome 10-year prison sentence for activist Joshua Wong amid int’l outcry
zh_title: “真实反映了他的罪行”：在国际社会的强烈抗议中，警方对活动人士黄之锋判处 10 年监禁表示欢迎
summary: 香港警务处国安处对黄之锋被判十年监禁表示欢迎，称这是反映所犯罪行的“适当刑罚”。 2026 年 11 月 5 日，黄之锋被判刑后，高等法院外的警察。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。香港警务处国家安全部总警司李锐周四在高等法院外对记者表示，希望这名活动人士刑满后能够正确了解中国，成为一个守法的人。黄伟
content:
香港警务处国安处对黄之锋被判十年监禁表示欢迎，称这是反映所犯罪行的“适当刑罚”。 2026 年 11 月 5 日，黄之锋被判刑后，高等法院外的警察。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。香港警务处国家安全部总警司李锐周四在高等法院外对记者表示，希望这名活动人士刑满后能够正确了解中国，成为一个守法的人。自 2020 年底以来一直入狱的黄在 9 月份承认与外国势力合谋罪名后，于周四被判处 10 年监禁。黄被指控在2020年与自我流亡的活动人士罗冠聪和其他未透露姓名的人士密谋，要求外国对香港和中国大陆政府实施制裁和封锁。活动家黄之锋于 2019 年 9 月 17 日在国会及行政部门中国委员会作证。照片：C-SPAN 屏幕截图。谭威廉法官周四表示，根据北京实施的国家安全法，此案性质“严重”，可判处至少 10 年监禁、最高无期徒刑。
当被《香港自由报》问及当局是否会上诉寻求更重的刑罚时，李说：“[判决]确实反映了他在此期间所犯的罪行，以及罪行的严重性。当然，我必须与司法部的同事讨论我们是否会[上诉]，但我个人认为这对他来说是一个适当的判决。”香港自由派获得了黄从监狱发出的一份声明，黄说，一名国安警察告诉他，他们是“敌人”。当被问及当局是否认为黄是敌人时，李说这不是他的观点。 2026 年 11 月 5 日，黄之锋在高等法院宣判后，警察国家安全局总警司李志强向新闻界发表讲话。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 “我个人不会把他视为敌人。他是一个罪犯。作为警察，我们需要做一些事情来纠正这种情况并加强法律，”李说。行政长官李家超在周四的一份声明中将黄罗及其附属公司描述为“破坏香港繁荣稳定的罪魁祸首之一”。 “惩罚异见的工具”黄目前正在服刑四年零八个月，罪名是在具有里程碑意义的“香港47”案件中串谋颠覆国家政权，该案中45名著名的民主运动人士被定罪，并于2024年被判处最高10年监禁。
谭法官下令新的 10 年徒刑与他现有刑期的剩余两个月零两天同时执行。因此，这位 30 岁的活动人士将于 2036 年 11 月获释，届时他将年满 40 岁。2026 年 11 月 5 日黄之锋宣判后，高等法院外的警察。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。国际特赦组织在周四发布的一份声明中表示，香港当局将一名为权力说真话的年轻人定为罪犯。该人权组织区域副主任莎拉·布鲁克斯(Sarah Brooks)表示，这一判决“残酷地——也许是故意的——是在他根据之前的定罪获得释放的几个月前做出的。” “

【原文 English Original】
The National Security Department of the Hong Kong Police Force has welcomed the 10-year prison sentence handed to Joshua Wong , saying that it was a “proper sentence” to reflect the offence committed. Police officers outside the High Court after Joshua Wong’s sentencing on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Steve Li, chief superintendent of the National Security Department of the Hong Kong Police Force, told reporters on Thursday outside the High Court that he hoped the activist would gain a proper understanding of China and become a law-abiding person after serving his sentence. Wong, who has been behind bars since late 2020, was sentenced to another 10 years in jail on Thursday after he pleaded guilty in September to conspiring to collude with foreign forces. Wong was accused of conspiring with self-exiled activist Nathan Law and other unnamed individuals in 2020 to request that foreign countries impose sanctions and blockades against the governments of Hong Kong and mainland China. Acitivist Joshua Wong testified before Congressional-Executive Commission on China on September 17, 2019. Photo: C-SPAN screenshot. Judge William Tam said on Thursday that the case was of a “grave nature” under the Beijing-imposed national security law, which warrants at least 10 years’ imprisonment and a maximum of life imprisonment. When asked by HKFP whether authorities would appeal to seek a heavier sentence, Li said: “[The sentence] is truly reflective of his offence committed during the period, of the grave nature of the offence. Of course, I have to discuss with DOJ [Department of Justice] colleagues whether we will [appeal], but personally I think it is a proper sentence to him.” In a statement sent by Wong from prison and obtained by HKFP, Wong said a national security police officer told him that they were “enemies.” When asked whether authorities considered Wong an enemy, Li said that was not his perspective. Chief Superintendent Steve Li of the police’s National Security Department speaks to the press after Joshua Wong’s sentencing at the High Court on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “I personally won’t regard him as an enemy. He is an offender. And as police officers, we need to do the things to rectify the situation and to reinforce the law,” Li said. In a statement on Thursday, Chief Executive John Lee described Wong, Law and their affiliates as “among the primary culprits responsible for undermining Hong Kong’s prosperity and stability.” ‘A tool to punish dissent’ Wong is currently serving a four-year, eight-month jail term for conspiracy to subvert state power imposed in the landmark “Hong Kong 47” case , in which 45 prominent pro-democracy campaigners were convicted and sentenced to up to 10 years in jail in 2024. Judge Tam ordered that the new 10-year prison term run concurrently with the remaining two months and two days of his existing sentence. The 30-year-old activist is thus due to be released in November 2036, when he will be 40. Police officers outside the High Court after Joshua Wong’s sentencing on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. In a statement released on Thursday, Amnesty International said that the Hong Kong authorities had made a young man who spoke truth to power a criminal. Sarah Brooks, deputy regional director of the human rights organisation, said that the sentence “cruelly – and perhaps deliberately – comes mere months before he would have been eligible for release under his previous conviction.” “Today’s sentence is another grim reminder of how Hong Kong’s National Security Law has become a tool to punish dissent rather than to genuinely protect national security… Amnesty International reiterates its call on the Hong Kong authorities to overturn Joshua Wong’s national security convictions and to repeal all legislation that violates Hong Kong’s international human rights obligations,” the statement reads. ‘Properly understand’ China Having first emerged in the public eye as an opponent of a government-proposed national education scheme, Wong formed the student activist group Scholarism in 2011. He quickly rose to prominence as a youth activist, later becoming a key student leader during the 2014 Umbrella Movement. Nathan Law. Photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. In 2016, Wong co-founded the political party Demosisto with Nathan Law, who ran in the legislative election representing the party and was elected as the city’s youngest lawmaker. Li said on Thursday that Law, who now resides in the United Kingdom, should hand himself in to the Hong Kong police as soon as possible. The national security police chief also said that Wong had committed various offences since he began participating in social movements. Former Scholarism activists Louis Lee and Tiffany Chin at the High Court after Joshua Wong’s sentencing on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “He started taking part in the social movement whilst he was a youngster, and has committed various offences since his adulthood, including his offence under the national security laws, and the organising and inciting unlawful assembly, and also the contempt of law in various occasions.” “I sincerely hope that for the rest of his time in the prison, apart from reflecting on the wrongdoings he has done to the country and to the HKSAR, he must seize opportunities, to learn how to respect the law and to properly understand his own country.”

content:
本周末依然有不少法国民众在巴黎等地抗议高昂生活成本、教育系统积弊等问题图像来源: Stephanie Lecocq/REUTERS
（德国之声中文网）法国多地民众本周末再次响应工会、青年组织、“黄马甲运动”发出的抗议号召。根据组织者的说法，全国共有25万人参加了11月7日的抗议活动；而法国内政部公布的数据则为14.6万人。而在上周六，抗议人数规模在32万至50万人。11月5日（周四）的罢工示威活动也有约60万人参加（内政部数据）。
在巴黎市中心，警方动用催泪弹试图驱散在禁止示威区域聚集的抗议者图像来源: Geoffroy Van Der Hasselt/AFP
法国内政部表示，在图卢兹、马赛、里昂、波尔多和斯特拉斯堡等主要城市，集会过程中出现了动荡及各类事件。在巴黎，游行本身保持了和平，但傍晚时分局势趋于紧张；现场画面显示出现了催泪瓦斯烟雾和火光。内政部报告称全国共有200余人被捕。
为保护市中心区域，多个城市都在部分街区实施示威禁令。比如在第二大城市里昂，据媒体报道，民众在未经官方许可的情况下聚集抗议，警方随即动用了催泪瓦斯。
在巴黎，“黄马甲运动”原计划举行的一场集会被禁止，而由工会组织的一场示威活动则获准进行。尽管如此，在“黄马甲运动”发出行动号召后，仍有不少人聚集在市中心的协和广场。据法国媒体报道，两名“黄马甲运动”的协调员在巴黎被捕。
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
法国民众正在抗议高昂生活成本、教育系统积弊等多项议题。法国全国学生联合会(UNEF)秘书长莫雷(Manon Moret)表示，年轻人依然态度坚决且感到愤怒，并指出政府未能回应他们的诉求。
法国总理塞巴斯蒂安·勒科尔尼(Lecornu)计划在11月9日与工会及雇主协会举行一场社会议题会议，并和中学生、大学生代表进行磋商。此外，11月10日也有计划举行进一步的抗议活动。

德国30多个城市周六举行青年抗议活动，数万名年轻人借此表达对教育资源、生活成本及环境保护等问题的不满。然而，原本大体和平的示威活动在晚间演变为多地暴力骚乱。
意大利数万学生和工人上街，要求增加教育经费、缓解生活成本压力。
说中文的骚扰电话并不少见，幸亏真正上钩的人并不多。《波恩汇报》近日报道了一名中国年轻女性被诈骗5万多欧的事件。

content:
2024年9月4日，巴布亚新几内亚首都莫尔兹比港一家购物中心外的标牌。
最近一个星期，中国与南太平洋岛国巴布亚新几内亚(巴新)因为一件酷似爆炸物的不明物体而引发一场外交风波。中国驻巴新大使馆称那是一个酒瓶，而巴新警方及军方坚持认为那是一枚未引爆的炮弹。
10月30日，有人在巴新首都莫尔兹比港的一个商用集装箱内，发现一枚重达32公斤的军绿色圆柱体物品。警方和军方爆炸物专家到场将这枚看似炮弹的物体妥善控制，并将其带走进行分析研究。
根据澳大利亚广播公司(ABC)的报道，巴新爆炸物专家星期二证实，藏匿在商用集装箱内的不明物体实际上是一枚未引爆的中国产五九式130毫米加农炮的炮弹，而且弹体内装填了化学炸药和引信。
同一天，中国驻巴新大使馆在社交媒体上X发表声明，否认不明物体是一枚未爆炮弹。
“据相关公司反馈，经现场核实，此前被报道为‘炮弹’的物体，实际上是一个炮弹形状的酒瓶，它完全不构成任何危险。”
星期五，中国驻巴新大使馆在X平台重新将这份声明再贴了一遍。
中国大使馆还试图淡化中国制造的军用武器被非法运入巴布亚新几内亚的可能性，声称鉴于中国严格的枪支管制法律，“非法将军用级炮弹从中国走私到巴布亚新几内亚，几乎是不可能的”。
59式130毫米加农炮是中国在1959年仿制苏制 M-46型130毫米加农炮研制成功的一款主力野战加农炮，主要用于杀伤敌方有生力量、摧毁防御工事、反坦克作战或压制敌方炮兵群。
不过，随着2012年中国军队体制编制调整，大部分传统的59式牵引加农炮已从一线精锐部队退役，部分转入封存、民兵预备役或移交至沿海的海防/岸防部队管理与使用。
巴新媒体《信使邮报》(Post-Courier)上星期五率先报道了此事。报道说，该不明物体是在一个建筑工地的集装箱内、建筑材料之间被发现的。
巴新警察局长戴维·曼宁(David Manning)称，警方与军方随后展开了联合调查，并排除了该物体可能是用于训练的“模拟弹”（假弹）的说法。
“警方在接到发现炮弹的消息后迅速采取了行动。相关区域已被封锁，以防对周边地区造成危害，”《每日电讯报》援引曼宁的话说。“这使得警方和军方的爆炸物处置专家得以进入现场，对该装置进行检查，并将其安全转移至一处稳妥的设施内进行存放。”
巴新警方尚未就中国大使馆提出的说法作出回应。不过，一些网民社交媒体上对中方的说法提出了质疑。
目前与此案有关而被捕的中国公民仍被扣押在莫尔兹比港。
近年来，中国持续扩大与包括巴新在内的南太平洋岛国之间的政治、经济和安全关系，不仅推动所罗门群岛与台湾断交，而且还与其签署了一份秘密安全协议。其他与台湾断交并与北京建交的南太国家还有瑙鲁和基里巴斯。
北京在南太平洋岛国扩充影响力的行为，引起美国、澳大利亚、新西兰等国的警觉。
针对此次中国“酒瓶与炮弹”事件，美国驻莫尔斯比港大使馆也在社媒X平台上发表评论说，美国国防官员与负责检查该物品的巴布亚新几内亚爆炸物处理小组进行了直接对接。
“这是一起严重的公共安全事件。巴布亚新几内亚人民有权获得准确的信息，并应进行彻底的调查，”美国大使馆的声明说。
“我们赞赏巴布亚新几内亚警方及国防人员所采取的应对行动，”美方声明又说，“美国与巴布亚新几内亚站在一起，共同维护其人民安全、国家安全及主权。”

Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

content:
香港环境局局长将出席在土耳其举行的联合国气候峰会 |中国劳工公告栏
2026 年 11 月 9 日星期一 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
香港环境局局长将出席在土耳其举行的联合国气候峰会
香港环境生态局局长谢展云将前往土耳其安塔利亚，与中国代表团一起出席第31届联合国气候变化大会。他将在中国方面的活动上发表讲话，并就该市的碳减排和气候战略举行双边会议。
香港环境生态局局长谢展云将于今晚离港前往土耳其安塔利亚，与中国代表团一起出席《联合国气候变化框架公约》第三十一届缔约方会议。
在气候峰会上，谢霆锋将在中国馆举行的一场边会上发表演讲。他亦会与其他与会代表举行双边会议，介绍香港在减碳和应对气候变化方面的策略和进展。
环境生态局气候变化专员杨秀娟及其他局员陪同出访。谢定于11月13日下午返港。
在他缺席期间，环境生态局副局长黄淑娴将代理局长职务。

Hong Kong environment chief to attend UN climate summit in Turkey
Hong Kong's Secretary for Environment and Ecology Tse Chin-wan will leave for Antalya, Turkey, to join the Chinese delegation at the 31st UN Climate Change Conference. He will speak at a China side event and hold bilateral meetings on the city's carbon reduction and climate strategies.
Hong Kong's Secretary for Environment and Ecology, Tse Chin-wan, will leave the city tonight to travel to Antalya, Turkey, where he will join the Chinese delegation attending the 31st session of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.
At the climate summit, Tse will deliver a speech at a side event held in the China Pavilion. He will also hold bilateral meetings with other participating representatives to present Hong Kong's strategies and progress in carbon reduction and climate change response.
The Commissioner for Climate Change of the Environment and Ecology Bureau, Yang Sau-kuen, and other bureau officials will accompany the secretary on the trip. Tse is scheduled to return to Hong Kong on the afternoon of 13 November.
During his absence, Deputy Secretary for Environment and Ecology Wong Suk-han will serve as acting secretary.

title: The ‘Invade the World, Invite the World’ Election
zh_title: “入侵世界，邀请世界”选举
summary: 政治 “入侵世界，邀请世界”的选举 如果不颠覆一个国家的政治，就无法改变一个国家的人口结构。由于选民对伊朗战争及其经济后果感到沮丧，共和党在中期选举中遭受重创，甚至包括副总统 J.D. 万斯在内的许多共和党人也承认这一点。但民主党取得如此规模的压倒性胜利是由另一个因素促成的：过去几十年来，美国的种族人口结构转型主要是由大规模移民推动的。如果只有白人投票，共和党就会有
content:
政治 “入侵世界，邀请世界”的选举 如果不颠覆一个国家的政治，就无法改变一个国家的人口结构。由于选民对伊朗战争及其经济后果感到沮丧，共和党在中期选举中遭受重创，甚至包括副总统 J.D. 万斯在内的许多共和党人也承认这一点。但民主党取得如此规模的压倒性胜利是由另一个因素促成的：过去几十年来，美国的种族人口结构转型主要是由大规模移民推动的。如果只有白人投票，共和党就会加强对参议院、众议院和州级办公室的控制。如果只有非白人投票的话，那么，连中共都会羡慕民主党的绝对统治地位。正如右翼社会评论家史蒂夫·塞勒（Steve Sailer）的名言，“入侵世界，邀请世界”，他总结了我们无能的领导层的军事和移民政策。这就是这次选举的故事。佐治亚州曾经是一个红宝石色的州，已经从 1990 年白人占绝对多数的州变成了今天白人占少数的州。因此，尽管乔治亚州白人大幅支持共和党候选人，桃州还是将乔恩·奥索夫送回参议院，并选举凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯担任州长，两人都是民主党人。德克萨斯州——传统上由共和党控制的人口最多的州——的结果更加令人震惊。但数据讲述了相同的基本情况。
德克萨斯州只有37%是白人，这也是民主党在孤星州占据主导地位的一个重要原因。倾向相当保守的德克萨斯州拉美裔不仅变蓝，而且人数众多。堪萨斯州、俄亥俄州、南卡罗来纳州，这样的例子不胜枚举，但你明白了。可以肯定的是，如果特朗普政府在过去两年里治理得更有能力——特别是如果它没有发动灾难性的伊朗战争——那么白人和非白人就不会像他们那样强烈地转向民主党，共和党也可能保住参议院。但这还不是故事的全部。美国的种族多样性为其选举奠定了背景，而这种背景对共和党来说越来越难以驾驭。我在印刷品和网络上（以及再次在网上）指出，由于美国人口结构的变化，民主党正在走向永久多数。很少有人同意我的分析——甚至经典著作《新兴的民主多数》（2002）的作者也否认了他们书中的论点——但我毫不怀疑。如果您仍然持怀疑态度，请思考一下这两个事实：1）自赫伯特·胡佛以来，还没有共和党总统候选人赢得过任何非白人种族群体的多数选票，2）到 2045 年左右，美国将成为非白人占多数的国家。反思完了吗？这是另一个事实：两党之间白人的分歧仍然比其他种族群体更大。
由白人自由主义者和非白人组成的民主党联盟如果成立，将在美国选民变成少数派之前数年实现稳定的统治。有几个因素减缓了民主党永久多数派的出现。投票的选民比一般人口更白。红队偶尔可以赢得超过 40% 的拉美裔选民，这是美国最大的少数族裔群体。许多未受过大学教育的白人已经逃往共和党，部分原因是对民主党的跨性别主义等精品文化迷恋的反应。以及反多数主义机构——格里姆

【原文 English Original】
Politics The ‘Invade the World, Invite the World’ Election You can’t transform a nation’s demographics without upending its politics. The Republican Party got smacked in the midterm elections because of voter frustration over the Iran War and its economic consequences, as even many Republicans, including Vice President J.D. Vance, have acknowledged. But the scale of the Democrats’ sweeping victory was enabled by another factor: America’s racial-demographic transformation over the past several decades, driven largely by mass migration. If only whites had voted, the Republican Party would have strengthened its hold on the Senate, the House of Representatives, and state-level offices. If only nonwhites had voted, well, even the Chinese Communists would envy the Democratic Party its utter dominance. “Invade the world, invite the world,” as the right-wing social commentator Steve Sailer famously put it, summarizing our inept leadership’s military and immigration policies. That’s the story of this election. Georgia, once a ruby-red state, has gone from being supermajority white in 1990 to minority white today. So even though white Georgians favored the Republican candidates by wide margins, the Peach State sent Jon Ossoff back to the Senate and elected Keisha Lance Bottoms as governor, both Democrats. The results in Texas—the most populous state traditionally held by the GOP—were even more shocking. But the data tell the same basic story. Only 37 percent of Texans are white, which is a big reason why Democrats dominated in the Lone Star State. Texas Hispanics, who tend to be fairly conservative, not only shifted blue but turned out in large numbers. Kansas, Ohio, South Carolina, the list goes on and on, but you get the idea. To be sure, if the Trump administration had governed more competently during the past two years—and especially if it hadn’t launched the disastrous Iran War—then whites and nonwhites alike wouldn’t have swung as sharply as they did toward the Democrats, and Republicans might have held onto the Senate. But that’s not the whole story. America’s racial diversity sets the context for its elections, and that context is an increasingly difficult one for Republicans to navigate. I’ve argued in print and online (and online again) that the Democrats are heading toward a permanent majority because of America’s changing demographics. Few people agree with my analysis—and even the authors of the classic text The Emerging Democratic Majority (2002) have disavowed their book’s thesis—but I harbor little doubt. If you remain skeptical, reflect on these two facts for a while: 1) No Republican presidential candidate since Herbert Hoover has won a majority of votes from any nonwhite racial group, and 2) America will be majority nonwhite by around 2045. Done reflecting? Here’s another fact: Whites remain more divided than other racial groups between the two parties. A Democratic coalition of white liberals and nonwhites, if it holds, will achieve stable domination years before America’s electorate turns majority-minority. Several factors have slowed the emergence of a permanent Democratic majority. The voting electorate is whiter than the general population. The Red Team can occasionally win more than 40 percent of Hispanics, America’s largest minority group. Many non-college-educated whites have fled to the GOP, partly in reaction to the Democrats’ boutique cultural fixations like transgenderism. And countermajoritarian institutions—gerrymandering in the House, malapportionment in the Senate, and the electoral college—mostly benefit the Republicans. Some analysts, after Donald Trump’s dramatic victory in 2024, posited a new “multiracial coalition” that would keep the GOP in the game. It was wishful thinking. Trump made inroads with nonwhites, but he merely brought the GOP back to its George W. Bush numbers, more or less. The margin of error for Republican presidential candidates is apparently slim. In 2024, Trump mobilized blue-collar whites and did reasonably well among minorities. And yet, facing a disastrous candidate installed at the 11th hour, Trump won the popular vote by a smaller margin than Hillary Clinton in 2016. What transpired this week was a different matter altogether—an electoral backlash that some thought impossible in our age of polarization—and it will have long-lasting political consequences. The Dems will probably maintain their Senate majority over several election cycles, and if Texas just became solidly blue, Republicans won’t stand a chance at winning the White House in 2028. Of course, a permanent Democratic majority doesn’t mean an eternal one. Perhaps the Democratic Party will splinter between its moderate and progressive factions, or maybe a viable third party will emerge that, over time, replaces the GOP. On the other hand, in cities and states that long ago became majority nonwhite, the Democrats enjoy one-party rule, and governance generally suffers. A nation is its people, as right-wingers often say. And you can’t transform a nation without upending its politics. The post The ‘Invade the World, Invite the World’ Election appeared first on The American Conservative .

title: Police say linking mall cameras to AI facial recognition network complies with Hong Kong privacy laws
zh_title: 警方表示，将商场摄像头连接到人工智能面部识别网络符合香港隐私法
summary: 警方表示，为香港的闭路电视网络配备人工智能面部识别软件并将其连接到购物中心的安全摄像头不会违反当地的隐私法。旺角的闭路电视摄像机。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。据当地媒体周五报道，警方表示，人工智能面部识别功能最早将于本月添加到该市的 SmartView 监控系统中，今年将有四家私人购物中心连接到该网络。据了解，这四间商场分别为大角咀奥海城、屯门市广场、葵涌商场及四二商场
content:
警方表示，为香港的闭路电视网络配备人工智能面部识别软件并将其连接到购物中心的安全摄像头不会违反当地的隐私法。旺角的闭路电视摄像机。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。据当地媒体周五报道，警方表示，人工智能面部识别功能最早将于本月添加到该市的 SmartView 监控系统中，今年将有四家私人购物中心连接到该网络。据当地媒体报道，这四家商场分别是大角咀的奥海城、屯门市广场、葵涌商场和粉岭的Sierra Life。警方行动科高级警司梁明亮表示，人工智能面部识别系统不会全天候运行，而是需要督察或以上级别的警官批准。 “我们首先要问的是，使用SmartView对于破案是否至关重要。必须审查多少个摄像头和多少镜头？这个范围是否符合调查目标？在批准任何申请之前，必须解决这些问题，”梁用粤语说。他表示，该技术将通过自动识别嫌疑人或失踪人员的面部是否在特定时间范围内的特定区域被摄像机捕捉到，帮助警察追查嫌疑人或失踪人员。梁补充说，或者，该系统可以实时追踪一个人的脸部，提醒警察他们出现的时间和地点。
闭路电视录像将在捕获后30天自动删除，而时间戳和位置等元数据将保留长达180天。“额外好处”梁还表示，根据警方法律团队和个人资料私隐专员的评估，与购物中心的连接不会违反隐私法。旺角的闭路电视摄像机。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 “这些商场已经配备了安全摄像头，通常与我们的 SmartView 系统具有相同的公共安全目的。连接到它们只是一个额外的好处，”他说。 SmartView项目于2024年启动，截至上个月，已帮助破获2,000起犯罪案件，并逮捕了约2,800名涉嫌谋杀和纵火等罪名的嫌疑人。当局的目标是到 2028 年，通过安装新摄像头并将私人系统和其他政府部门运营的系统连接到警察网络，将全市 60,000 个监控摄像头纳入该系统。 SmartView 第三阶段计划在 2028 年至 2031 年间再安装 6,500 个监控摄像头。

【原文 English Original】
Equipping Hong Kong’s CCTV network with AI facial recognition software and connecting it to shopping mall security cameras would not breach local privacy laws, police have said. A CCTV camera in Mong Kok. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Police have said that the AI facial recognition feature will be added to the city’s SmartView surveillance system as early as this month, with four private shopping malls set to be connected to the network this year, local media reported on Friday. The four malls are understood to be Olympian City in Tai Kok Tsui, Tuen Mun Town Plaza, Kwai Chung Shopping Centre, and Sierra Life in Fanling, local media reported . Leung Ming-leung, a senior superintendent in the police’s Operations Bureau, said the AI facial recognition system would not operate round-the-clock, but would instead require sign-off from an officer ranked inspector or above. “We first ask whether using SmartView is essential to solving the crime. How many cameras and how much footage must be reviewed? Does that scope align with the investigation’s objectives? These points must be settled before any application is approved,” Leung said in Cantonese. He said the technology would help officers track down suspects or missing persons by automatically identifying whether their faces had been caught on camera in a particular area during a specific timeframe. Alternatively, the system could trace an individual’s face in real time, alerting officers to when and where they appear, Leung added. The CCTV footage will be automatically deleted 30 days after capture, while metadata such as timestamps and locations will be retained for up to 180 days. ‘Added bonus’ Leung also said that the connections to shopping malls would not breach privacy laws, based on assessments by the police’s legal team and the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data. A CCTV camera in Mong Kok. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “These malls are already equipped with security cameras, often serving the same public safety purpose as our SmartView system. Linking into them is merely an added bonus,” he said. The SmartView project was launched in 2024 and, as of last month, had helped solve 2,000 crimes and led to the arrest of about 2,800 suspects on charges including murder and arson. Authorities aim to incorporate 60,000 surveillance cameras across the city into the system by 2028, by installing new cameras and linking private systems and those operated by other government departments to the police network. A further 6,500 surveillance cameras are planned between 2028 and 2031 under SmartView’s third phase.

title: Hong Kong installs HK$5m ‘anti-terrorism’ crash bollards outside Causeway Bay dep’t store
zh_title: 香港在铜锣湾百货商店外安装价值 500 万港元的“反恐”防撞柱
summary: 香港当局在香港最繁忙的购物区之一铜锣湾的一家百货公司外安装了“反恐”防撞柱，该项目耗资 500 万港元。 2026 年 11 月 6 日，铜锣湾的“反恐”交通路柱。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。周四早上，这些护柱仍被泡沫板包裹着，最初是由警方、运输部和路政部在一月份作为反恐工作组的一部分提出的。 500万港元的临时预算还包括维修费用
content:
香港当局在香港最繁忙的购物区之一铜锣湾的一家百货公司外安装了“反恐”防撞柱，该项目耗资 500 万港元。 2026 年 11 月 6 日，铜锣湾的“反恐”交通路柱。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。周四早上，这些护柱仍被泡沫板包裹着，最初是由警方、运输部和路政部在一月份作为反恐工作组的一部分提出的。根据提交给湾仔区议会的一份文件，500万港元的临时预算还包括护柱的维护费用。这些护柱计划安装在轩尼诗道 555 号外和百德新街沿线。 2026 年 11 月 6 日，铜锣湾崇光百货外的“反恐”交通标杆。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。会议记录显示，工作组建议安装60个防撞柱，其中固定式柱43个，伸缩式柱17个。 “护柱之间将留有足够的间距，以便轮椅、婴儿车和担架可以顺利通过，而不会受到阻碍，”它说。警方指出，铜锣湾是港岛区的“核心商业区和旅游区”，人流繁忙，“如果车辆在该地区冲撞人群，可能会造成严重伤亡。” 2026年11月6日，铜锣湾的“反恐”交通路柱。
照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。“通过这些设施，可以采用最直接的物理隔离方法，有效防止车辆故意冲撞行人专用区，从而最大限度地降低人员伤亡的风险。”崇光百货外的区域历史上曾是香港抗议活动的主要聚集区，距离天安门广场镇压守夜活动的旧址维多利亚公园仅一箭之遥。 2026 年 11 月 6 日，铜锣湾崇光百货外的“反恐”交通标杆。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。近年来，在6月4日镇压周年纪念日当天，警察在维多利亚公园和铜锣湾周围保持大量警力，拦截和拘留活动人士和进行象征性哀悼活动的个人。

Hong Kong authorities have installed “anti-terrorism” collision bollards outside a department store in Causeway Bay, one of the city’s busiest shopping districts – a project with a HK$5 million price tag. “Anti-terrorism” traffic bollards in Causeway Bay on November 6, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The bollards, which were still wrapped in foam sheeting on Thursday morning, were initially proposed in January by the police, the Transport Department, and the Highways Department as part of a counter-terrorism working group. The provisional budget of HK$5 million also includes maintenance costs for the bollards, according to a document submitted to the Wan Chai District Council. The bollards were planned for installation outside 555 Hennessy Road and along Paterson Street. “Anti-terrorism” traffic bollards outside Sogo in Causeway Bay on November 6, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Meeting records show that the working group proposed installing 60 anti-collision bollards, including 43 fixed bollards and 17 retractable ones. “Sufficient spacing would be left between the bollards so that wheelchairs, baby strollers and stretchers could pass through smoothly without being obstructed,” it said. Noting that Causeway Bay is a “core business district and tourist area” on Hong Kong Island with heavy foot traffic, the police said that “[i]f vehicles were to ram into crowds at the location, serious casualties could result.” “Anti-terrorism” traffic bollards in Causeway Bay on November 6, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “Through these facilities, the most direct physical separation method could be used to effectively prevent vehicles from deliberately ramming into pedestrian areas, thereby minimising the risk of casualties,” it said. The area outside the Sogo department store historically served as a major gathering zone for protests in Hong Kong, and is a stone’s throw away from Victoria Park, the former site of the city’s Tiananmen Square crackdown vigils. “Anti-terrorism” traffic bollards outside Sogo in Causeway Bay on November 6, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. In recent years, police officers have maintained a heavy presence around Victoria Park and Causeway Bay on the anniversary of the crackdown on June 4 , stopping and detaining activists and individuals who engaged in symbolic acts of mourning.

Fundraiser by Nurnisa Kurban : Uyghur Cultural Preservation and Survival Through Education
Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Nurnisa Kurban is organizing this fundraiser to benefit Uyghur Academic Foundation.
Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Uyghur Cultural Preservation and Survival Through Education
The Uyghur people have been persecuted and subjected to repressive Chinese government policies in their Indigenous homeland of East Turkestan for many years. It is estimated that up to three million Uyghurs have been interned, imprisoned, and enslaved in detention centers, prisons, and forced labor facilities throughout China since 2017.
In 2021, the Uyghur Tribunal found that China was committing genocide and other crimes against humanity against Uyghurs. In 2022, the United Nations also concluded that China was committing human rights violations against Uyghurs amounting to crimes against humanity. Countries including the United States, Canada, the Netherlands, Czech Republic, United Kingdom, Lithuania, Belgium, and France have all declared a genocide in East Turkestan. Despite these declarations of genocide and related reports by various human rights organizations, atrocities against Uyghurs continue today with very limited international recognition and accountability.
During this time of ongoing genocide and cultural erasure in their Indigenous homeland, Uyghurs of the diaspora are working to preserve their culture and identity as a matter of survival. Uyghur education has been eradicated by the Chinese State, Uyghur texts are forbidden and in danger of being eliminated, and the Uyghur language itself is prohibited.
Uyghur scholars, linguists, and other specialists in the diaspora worldwide serve on the Uyghur Language and Education Committee of the Uyghur Academy to preserve the work of Uyghur intellectuals who have been persecuted and forcibly disappeared. This work has been ongoing since 2009 and is continuing to expand.
The Committee has created standards-aligned K-5 textbooks, which include classic and contemperory Uyghur literature, poetry, historical texts, and biographies for Uyghur children to learn about their own culture and identity in their native language. The Committee is seeking funding to expand and revise the existing K-5 textbooks, create teacher’s edition textbooks for educators, and design supplemental resources. They also hope to develop Middle and High School textbooks and related supplemental resources. To effectively implement these educational materials, they would also like to provide training for teachers.
Please consider supporting this urgent work of the Uyghur Academic Foundation as a matter of cultural survival for future generations of the Uyghur people.

summary: 能说中文的电话中心（Callcenter）遍布世界各地图像来源: Tim Goode/PA Wire/picture alliance （德国之声中文网）今年9月2日，林（化名）的手机突然响起，来电告知是“中国大使馆”。接通后，电话那头声称，林的身份在中国被盗用，请赶紧报警。 20多岁的林同父母一道生活在德国西部城市波恩，是中国公民，但她的中国身份证放在国内，多年未使用。林想，身份证在国内被盗是可能的。 对方随即安排了报警，通过Microsoft Teams与一位自称“警官”
content:
能说中文的电话中心（Callcenter）遍布世界各地图像来源: Tim Goode/PA Wire/picture alliance
（德国之声中文网）今年9月2日，林（化名）的手机突然响起，来电告知是“中国大使馆”。接通后，电话那头声称，林的身份在中国被盗用，请赶紧报警。
20多岁的林同父母一道生活在德国西部城市波恩，是中国公民，但她的中国身份证放在国内，多年未使用。林想，身份证在国内被盗是可能的。
对方随即安排了报警，通过Microsoft Teams与一位自称“警官”的男子通话。打开摄像头后，画面中出现一位身穿警服、胸前印有编号的警察，男子实录下林的报案。当林说出真实姓名后，对方关掉摄像头，紧接着，对方问：“你为何不主动说自己卷入了这起案件？”
林开始怀疑对方的真实身份，第二天，男子又打开摄像头，带林“参观”了警察局。林看到办公桌，其他警员，门厅里有警察局徽章，门外的路牌上显示警察局的方向。
对方告诉林，一名持有600张银行卡的嫌疑人在一个机场被捕，其中一张卡写着林的姓名。他说，林的银行卡已被用于跨国洗钱。他要求林不要关闭手提电脑，称随时可以视讯通话。惶恐当中的林，甚至显示了她的银行流水单，“我没有什么可以隐瞒的”。
两周后，对方告知，上面发出对林的逮捕通知，若想不被逮捕，只能向检察官申请押金保释。按照林后来的叙述，对方向林显示对方当场向上级汇报的场景。
林害怕极了，开始借钱、贷款并汇往对方指定的香港和越南的账号。对方说，中国腐败太严重，而现在进行的调查必须保密。林还透露了她即将回国探亲，对方称，鉴于林的风险增大，还需另加赎金。林一共三次汇款，加起来约5.5万欧元。
一个巧合，让林有一天在德国电视一台看到一个诈骗报道，其中的诈骗术跟她自己的经历非常相似，都是假冒中国官员进行电话诈骗。于是，9月24日，林来到波恩一个警察局报案。
故事的结局还是多少有点令人欣慰，林汇给骗子的金额没有全部丢失，三笔汇款中有两笔被当地银行拒绝。
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
波恩警察局证实了以上案件的真实性，提醒在德国上学、工作的中国背景的人士，遇到类似事件立即报警，寻求咨询，不要继续接触可疑的对方。
据媒体报道，德国联邦刑警局在一份回复信函中指出，作案者说中文并假冒中国官员，并不能证实诈骗人员一定来自中国。能说中文的电话中心（Callcenter）遍布世界各地。
根据北威州的犯罪记录，说中文并针对中国背景的公民的诈骗活动，没有单独进行归类统计。在北威州，2023年至2026年的不完全统计记录了数起此类案件，总体呈下降趋势。

title: US Air Force eyes reviving WWII air bases in the Pacific
zh_title: 美国空军着眼于复兴太平洋地区的二战空军基地
summary: 据美国空军部发布的公告称，美国空军希望每年在西北太平洋三个美国岛屿上的四个机场执行超过 6000 架次的飞机行动，其中包括一个正在翻新的二战时期主要机场。该部门发布了一份准备环境影响报告的意向通知，该报告将评估塞班国际机场、天宁岛国际机场、天宁岛北机场和罗塔国际机场的培训和运营的“潜在社会、经济和环境影响”。岛屿
content:
据美国空军部发布的公告称，美国空军希望每年在西北太平洋三个美国岛屿上的四个机场执行超过 6000 架次的飞机行动，其中包括一个正在翻新的二战时期主要机场。该部门发布了一份准备环境影响报告的意向通知，该报告将评估塞班国际机场、天宁岛国际机场、天宁岛北机场和罗塔国际机场的培训和运营的“潜在社会、经济和环境影响”。这些岛屿是北马里亚纳群岛联邦的一部分，是美国的非建制领土。拟议的训练和演习将支持空军的敏捷作战作战概念，该概念强调部队在机场之间的分散以及在各种条件下维持作战的同时在机场之间进行机动的能力，目的是挫败对手通过瞄准单个基地来关闭这些作战的能力。众所周知，ACE 的发展很大程度上是为了应对中国军队不断扩大的影响力和不断扩大的导弹库。
通知称，这四个机场为支持 ACE 提供了“独特的机会”，其基础设施从“完全开发的商业机场到远征作战地点”各不相同。这三个岛屿彼此相距不到几十海里，这将允许进行反映分布式行动复杂性的训练，同时减少它们之间的运输时间。它们距离美国另一个领土关岛的主要军事基地以北不到100海里，该基地将为这些演习提供部队的集结和部署。通知中写道，这三个机场“共同提供了一个训练环境，使[空军]能够进行分布式作战、测试和使用可定制的部队包、加强保障和机动能力以及增强作战弹性”。环境影响报告将评估拟议活动的潜在影响，其中包括每年举行几次、每次为期几周的小型、中型和大型训练和演习，包括每年在每个机场进行多达 1,200 次固定翼和 320 次旋转翼操作，例如起飞和着陆。
它还将评估一种替代方案，即每个机场每年多达1,400次固定翼和384次旋转翼操作，以及“无行动替代方案”。“培训和演习将得到每个机场多达55万加仑的燃料的支持，每个机场多达1000人，临时安装远征基础设施，处理箔条和照明弹等弹药，以及支持服务和培训前后和演习活动。战后，北场不活跃，在2023年底开始修复工作时，主要覆盖着植被。空军还升级了港口和道路基础设施、燃料管道和机场表面以及公用事业，以促进天宁岛的扩张。机场修复工作在空军领导人中引起了一些关于资源和资金的问题，特别是在与伊朗的战争提出了新的要求

【原文 English Original】
The U.S. Air Force hopes to conduct more than 6,000 aircraft operations annually at four airfields on three American islands in the northwest Pacific Ocean, including a major WWII-era airfield that is being refurbished , according to an announcement from the Department of the Air Force. The department published a notice of intent to prepare an environmental impact statement that will assess “potential social, economic, and environmental effects” of training and operations at Saipan International Airport, Tinian International Airport, Tinian North Field and Rota International Airport. The islands are part of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, an unincorporated U.S. territory. The proposed training and exercises will support the Air Force’s Agile Combat Operations concept, which emphasizes dispersal of forces across airfields and the ability to maneuver between them while sustaining operations under a range of conditions, with the goal of thwarting an adversary’s ability to shut down those operations by targeting a single base. ACE, as it’s known, has developed largely in response to the Chinese military’s growing reach and expanding missile arsenal.  The notice said the four airfields provide “a unique opportunity” to support ACE, with infrastructure that varies from “fully developed commercial airfields to expeditionary operating locations.” The three islands are within a few dozen nautical miles of each other, which would allow for training that reflects the complexity of distributed operations while reducing transit time between them. They are less than 100 nautical miles north of the major military bases on Guam, another U.S. territory, which would support the staging and deployment of forces for those exercises. The three airfields “collectively provide a training environment that enables [the Air Force] to exercise distributed operations, test and employ tailorable force packages, strengthen sustainment and maneuver capabilities, and enhance operational resilience,” the notice reads. The environmental impact statement will evaluate the potential effects of the proposed activities, which include small, medium and large trainings and exercises held several times a year for a few weeks at a time and consisting of up to 1,200 fixed-wing and 320 rotary-wing operations, like takeoffs and landings, annually at each airfield. It will also assess an alternative scenario with up to 1,400 fixed-wing and 384 rotary-wing operations per airfield annually and a “No Action Alternative.” The trainings and exercises would be supported by up to 550,000 gallons of fuel at each airfield, up to 1,000 personnel per airfield, the temporary installation of expeditionary infrastructure, the handling of munitions like chaff and flares, as well as support services and pre-and post-training and exercise activities.  The proposed activity comes after several years of work to upgrade the airfields in question, especially the airfields on Tinian, which were built and heavily used during WWII. North Field was inactive after the war and was largely covered with vegetation when the rehabilitation effort began in late 2023. The Air Force also upgraded port and roadway infrastructure, fuel pipelines and airfield surfaces, and utilities to facilitate expanded operations on Tinian . The airfield rehabilitation efforts have created some questions among Air Force leaders about resourcing and funding, particularly as the war with Iran has placed new demands on the force. Island residents also have misgivings about the projects. While some welcome the investment that the construction and military operations will bring, others have doubts that the increased activity will really benefit the islands’ populations and that the Pentagon will be transparent about its activity and responsive to local concerns.  The Department of the Air Force will hold public meetings this month on Saipan, Tinian and Rota to get feedback on the proposal, with written comments due by Nov. 29. The department plans to produce a draft environmental impact statement for public comment in fall 2027 and a final version in mid-2028.
